efet_title: Product safety recall - Toyota Land Cruiser Prado, Lexus GX, Lexus UX and Jeep Grand Cherokee vehicles - The National Consumer Commission
efet_body:
Product safety recall – Toyota Land Cruiser Prado, Lexus GX, Lexus UX and Jeep Grand Cherokee vehicles
Date Posted:
September 23, 2026
The National Consumer Commission (NCC) notifies consumers about product recalls involving the Toyota Land Cruiser Prado, Lexus GX, Lexus UX and Jeep Grand Cherokee (WL) as notified by respective suppliers.
Toyota Land Cruiser Prado- 2 279 vehicles
Toyota SA Motors (PTY) Ltd, informed the NCC that the recall affects two thousand two hundred and seventy-nine (2279) vehicles that were made available from 5 December 2023 to 7 August 2025. The recall is due to a software error of the combination meter, during meter startup the 3D graphics Micro Controller Unit may not fully initialise resulting in a blank image in the 3D graphics area which is part of the meter. In this condition, the indicators for engine oil pressure, engine coolant temperature, electrical charge, and other warning messages may not display on the combination meter. The affected units were sold nationally through Toyota dealerships.
Jeep Grand Cherokee (WL)- 255 vehicles
The recall affects two hundred and fifty-five (255), of which two hundred and fifty-one (251) units were sold nationwide from 2023 to 2025. Four vehicles are still with the manufacturer. According to Stellantis South Africa, the Airbag Control Unit module on the affected modules may have been built containing software which may cause transient door airbag pressure sensor faults to remain active for the lifetime of the sensor. This may result in delayed deployment of the Side Air Bag (SAB). A delayed deployment of the SAB may reduce front seat occupant protection in the event of certain types of crashes, potentially resulting in an increased risk of injury to motor vehicle occupants.
Lexus GX and Lexus UX- 41 vehicles
Lexus SA Motors (PTY) Ltd (Lexus) also informed the NCC of the recall of Lexus GX and Lexus UX vehicles due to the Air Bag Control Unit module. According to Lexus, the module of the affected vehicles may have been built containing software which may cause transient door airbag pressure sensor faults to remain active for the lifetime of the sensor. This may result in delayed deployment of the SAB. This may reduce front seat occupant protection in the event of certain types of crashes, potentially resulting in an increased risk of injury to motor vehicle occupants. This recall affects a total of forty-one (41) units and were made available from 17 April 2024 to 08 September 2025 and sold nationally.
Consumers who own any of the affected vehicle are urged to immediately visit their nearest authorised dealership to arrange for an inspection and repair. Any corrective work relating to this recall will be carried out at no cost to the consumer.
Questions and queries relating to this recall may be directed to: ProductRecall@thencc.org.za.
Ends

efet_title: Media Statement: Deli Hummus range Product Safety Recall - The National Consumer Commission
efet_body:
Media Statement: Deli Hummus range Product Safety Recall
Date Posted:
October 3, 2024
On 16 September 2024, Shoprite Checkers notified the Consumer Commission (NCC) of a product recall of the Deli Hummus range manufactured by BM Foods (a member of Sea Harvest Group), following the detection of Listeria Monocytogenes which is a species of foodborne bacteria.
The affected products are the Deli Hummus range, specifically the following:
Traditional Hummus (125g and 300g);
Reduced Fat Hummus (125g);
Zataar Hummus (125g and 300g);
Red Pepper Hummus (125g and 300g); and
Caramelised Onion Hummus (125g).
The respective sell-by dates of the products are 10 September 2024 to 08 October 2024.
Subsequent to the product recall notification, and in line with Section 60 of the Consumer Protection Act 68 of 2008, Shoprite Checkers has now provided an interim Investigation Report to the NCC on the Deli Hummus range. The preliminary findings of the report point to some areas of concern on product handling at the manufacturing level, however, the NCC awaits a final report from Shoprite Checkers. Parallel to the said in-house processes, the NCC is independently investigating the recalled products on identified operational issues that pertain to food safety.
The NCC’s Acting Commissioner, Mr. Hardin Ratshisusu, urged consumers to immediately stop consuming the products and return same to the supplier for a full refund with or without any proof of purchase. He further added that “at this stage, the NCC is not able to determine the extent of the distribution of the products as this is the subject of an investigation. Suppliers are urged not to distribute these products further until the investigation is finalised.”
The NCC is monitoring this recall based on the Product Recall provisions of the Consumer Protection Action read with the product recall safety guidelines.
ENDS
Issued by: National Consumer Commission (NCC)

efet_title: Product Recall: Consumers are urged to return certain Mercedes-Benz vehicles
efet_body:
Product Recall: Consumers urged to return certain Mercedes-Benz
vehicles Date Posted: June 10, 2022 Product Recall: Consumers are urged to return certain Mercedes-Benz vehicles. The National Consumer Commission (NCC) urges consumers who are in possession of Mercedes-Benz ML, GL, (model series 164) and R-Class (model series 251) to stop driving these vehicles and contact Mercedes-Benz for further assistance. To contact The National Consumer Commission about this and other Product Recalls , you can use any of the channels that can be found on our Contact page.
